key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow maps thermodynamic stability across hybrid perovskite alloy composition space, showing that stable regions are much narrower in Sn-based alloys than in Pb-based ones.
engineering_relevance: The results identify high-iodide compositions as the most promising targets and provide design guidance for more stable alloyed perovskite solar absorbers.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data perform fast structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed quaternary-alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes are computed across composition and phase, including alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates phase stability landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, finding maximum stability at high I content and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Predicted stability trends depend on ML models trained from DFT data, so transferability to unseen chemistries or extreme compositions may need additional validation.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
